title: Brighton’s James Milner unsure whether he will continue playing next season
content:
James Milner is unsure whether he will carry on playing next season after setting a new Premier League record of 654 appearances.

The 40-year-old midfielder, who broke Gareth Barry’s record of 653 games by starting Brighton & Hove Albion’s 2-0 win at Brentford last Saturday, is out of contract in June.

Milner is more interested in the team than personal achievements, but he would become the oldest Premier League outfield player by adding to his tally in October next season, overtaking Teddy Sheringham’s mark of 40 years and 272 days.

“I think things change very quickly in football, and I think when you get to my age things change very quickly as well.” said Milner, whose career was nearly ended by a knee injury last season. “When I look at where I was last year, not being able to lift my foot for six months, to where I am this year, and even where I was maybe six weeks ago where I wasn’t playing too many minutes and things aren’t going too well and you’re frustrated, and then I’ve played more minutes the last two games and you’ve played part in a win, it’s easier to turn around and say, ‘Yes, I’d love to do another year.’

“I’m pretty open at this moment in time, whether I will or whether I won’t, I’m not sure. We haven’t had any conversations, so obviously the club have to be interested as well.”

Brighton’s head coach Fabian Hurzeler told The Athletic in January that he wants Milner to stay on next season.

Asked whether he fears retirement, Milner said: “No, I wouldn’t say I fear it. I think it’s a tough question to know when’s the right time, because I feel like I still can do it now, but do you go to the point where you can’t? Is that too long? At the finish of the (Brentford) game some of the boys said ‘you can’t retire Millie this year, you’ve got to go again next year’. So I think that’s always a tough decision, to get the right time.

“But Jurgen (Klopp) always said, whenever you finish, you need to have a rest and a break straight away and I think that’s pretty appealing at this moment in time.

“I look forward to having that break and having time to do what I want, but most people say you miss the structure and training. When you haven’t got that, I think I’d probably look towards doing marathons or something like that to give me something to go for again.”

Milner is leaning towards a move into management when his playing days are over.

“Sometimes it appeals to me, for sure,” he said, speaking to reporters at Brighton’s training ground in Lancing. “And then other times, you see managers getting a new contract and getting sacked in two months, things like that, and I just don’t think people get the time they deserve now.

“When I look at managers and clubs and successful teams, they’ve been given patience and you’ve got two, three windows where it’s your team and you’ve got a whole other team that you then need to get your players, get your ideas across, get the culture across. So, there’s some times I think, yes, it would be great and I’d love to put my stamp on a team and I think I could do this and that.

“I know it’s difficult but I feel as though I’ve got a fantastic knowledge of people I’ve worked under, from Terry Venables and Bobby Robson through to the current manager now. I’ve got a great array of different managers from different countries and different personalities to lean back on, so in one way I think it would be a big shame to lose all that knowledge and experience I’ve built up without using it.”
